requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.
verdict_reason: the requirement has 2 plausible readings that lead to different code; a named human must choose

Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed

Regeneration: 222/222 generated files verified by 89 passing snapshot tests on head

findings.claim: Adding ExcludeFromCodeCoverage to the generated partial declaration of a user-declared resolver breaks resolvers that already have that attribute. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute does not allow multiples, so the attributes from the user's and generated partial declarations merge and produce CS0579, turning a reasonable pre-upgrade workaround into a compile error.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedExcludeFromCodeCoverageTests.ExistingExcludeFromCodeCoverageOnResolverDoesNotDuplicateAttribute. Its source declares a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial resolver that is already decorated with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]; compilation succeeds on base and should fail on head with an unexpected CS0579 duplicate-attribute diagnostic.

hunches.claim: The per-type coverage assertion is only per-file: it passes when a generated file contains one attribute, so removing ExcludeFromCodeCoverage from FormatterCache<T> or the resolver's GetFormatterHelper is not detected even though the test claims every generated type is decorated.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs:52-54 delete-statement: the guarded ExcludeFromCodeCoverage emission on FormatterCache<T> -> removed; expected to survive because AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage uses text.Contains(ExcludeAttribute) for the whole file, and the resolver class still supplies one matching occurrence.

hunches.claim: The target-framework test checks preprocessor text but never compiles the generated output with target-framework symbols. RunGeneratorsAndUpdateCompilation discards both the output compilation and diagnostics, so malformed generated syntax or an unavailable attribute can satisfy the acceptance-critical compilation requirement unnoticed.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile the output compilation for a modern target with no exclusion symbols and for netstandard2.0/.NET Framework with NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK defined in CSharpParseOptions, using matching references, and assert no compilation diagnostics; verify the test fails when the guard is removed or generated attribute placement is malformed.

refused.what: Which reading of REQ-2297 is intended (A or B)
refused.why: 3 of 3 independent readers found two readings: A: Decorate every generated type—including formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, and resolvers—with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally and provide no setting; B: Apply ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally only to generated formatter types, leaving non-formatter generated code such as resolvers without the attribute; the requirement says: 'Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open'.

residual_risk: This change touches 237 files (222 generated) in codegen-templates, tests; the highest routed risk is 7/10. 14 file(s) were routed for deep review, 1 for light review and 222 to the regeneration check. The existing source generator tests ran on head: 169 of 169 passed, 0 failed. 2 unverified hunch(es) remain without an executed receipt. It touches risky areas (codegen-templates), so a human must sign off. 6 thing(s) were not checked, including mutation testing; generated formatter bytes (source generator output, base vs head); compatibility byte diff (base vs head serialized bytes). By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The AI did not choose between the readings; whoever merges A or B owns that product decision and the receipts of the branch they merge.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate every generated type—including formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, and resolvers—with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally and provide no setting. Code: Update all relevant source-generator transforms so every emitted generated type receives the attribute, conditionally emitting it only as needed for target-framework compatibility, and update all affected verified snapshots; unlike the narrower reading, resolver and other non-formatter generated types are included, and unlike the opt-out reading no configuration API is added.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Apply ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally only to generated formatter types, leaving non-formatter generated code such as resolvers without the attribute. Code: Change the formatter-related transforms and their snapshots but not resolver or other generated-type templates; the emitted coverage behavior and scope of modified snapshots differ from the all-generated-types reading.
